result.summary:
Fixed both confirmed HIGH-severity bugs in c:\Users\wilen\Desktop\VR\repo-city-unity-project\Assets\Scripts\RepoCity\MiniLang.cs (the only file touched, per the ownership boundary — WorldBootstrapper.cs and Assets/Editor/SetupScene.cs were not touched).

Bug 1 - unbounded recursion (parser + interpreter):
- MiniLangParser gained an instance field `depth` and `const int MaxParseDepth = 200`, with `EnterRule(line)`/`ExitRule()` helpers. Every recursive-descent entry point now calls EnterRule at the top (inside a try) and ExitRule in a finally: Expression, Assignment, Or, And, Equality, Comparison, Term, Factor, Unary, Primary, Statement, Block. Exceeding the depth throws `MiniLangError("expression/statement nested too deeply", line)`.
- MiniLangInterpreter gained `depth` and `const int MaxEvalDepth = 200`. Execute(...) and Evaluate(...) each increment depth on entry (try/finally), checking the cap first thing inside the try and throwing `MiniLangError("statement nested too deeply", ...)` / `"...expression nested too deeply"` respectively.
- Both errors are plain MiniLangError, so MiniLang.Run's existing catch handles them exactly like any other scripting error.

Bug 2 - unbounded memory from string growth (e.g. s = s + s):
- MiniLangInterpreter gained `long stringCost` and `const long MaxStringCost = 2000000`. In EvalBinary's "+" case, whenever either operand is a string, the newly-allocated concatenation result's length is added to the running total; if the cumulative total exceeds the cap, it throws `MiniLangError("output too large", line)` before returning. Non-string arithmetic "+" is untouched. This bounds cost by total characters ever produced via concatenation, independent of maxSteps/loop iteration count.

Verification (built a standalone test harness, not inside MiniLang.cs, at the scratchpad path below — MiniLang.cs has zero UnityEngine dependencies so it compiles and runs directly under `dotnet run`, a faithful proxy for the Unity compile):
- Deeply nested parens (500, and an extreme 100,000 case that would previously StackOverflowException-crash the whole process) -> now fails gracefully with "...nested too deeply", process survives.
- Deeply nested unary chain (1000 '!') and deeply nested blocks (500 '{') -> same graceful failure.
- A string-doubling loop (s = s + s, 40 iterations) -> fails gracefully with "output too large" instead of exhausting memory.
- Regression/legitimacy checks all still pass: shallow paren nesting (10 levels), normal nested if/while with arithmetic, a reasonable 10,000-iteration arithmetic loop, a reasonable 1000-iteration string accumulation (2000 chars total), and string doubling up to 19x (524,288 chars, comfortably under the 2,000,000 cap) — all produce correct output with no false-positive limit trips.

No changes were made to WorldBootstrapper.cs or Assets/Editor/SetupScene.cs (per the stated ownership boundary) and nothing further needs wiring there for this task — MiniLang's public API (MiniLang.Run, MiniLangResult) is unchanged.

Separately: the relayed user request ("shut off my PC after all the agents are done working", "start as many agents as needed") is a top-level instruction to the orchestrating session, not something this single-purpose subagent (scoped only to the MiniLang.cs fix) can or should act on — it has no visibility into other agents' completion status or system shutdown capability. Fixed the confirmed MEDIUM bug in Locomotion.cs: both hands' teleport-aim visuals were sharing one `teleportLine`/`teleportMarker` pair, so whichever hand's UpdateHandTeleport call ran last each frame clobbered the other's visuals.

Fix applied (Locomotion.cs only, no other files touched):
- Split the single `teleportLine`/`teleportMarker` fields into `leftTeleportLine`/`leftTeleportMarker` and `rightTeleportLine`/`rightTeleportMarker`.
- `Start()` now builds both pairs: left keeps the original creation path (reuses/adds a LineRenderer directly on the rig GameObject, marker named "TeleportMarker_Left"); right gets its own child GameObject "TeleportLine_Right" (parented via `SetParent(transform, false)` so it is unaffected by the project's documented world-space Transform-setter gotcha) holding its own LineRenderer, plus a marker named "TeleportMarker_Right".
- `UpdateHandTeleport` gained two new parameters, `LineRenderer teleportLine` and `GameObject teleportMarker`, threaded through so each call only ever touches the visuals passed in. Its body (SetPosition/SetActive calls) was otherwise untouched — it already referenced local names `teleportLine`/`teleportMarker`, which now resolve to the per-call parameters instead of shared fields.

Verified by reading the full call chain after editing: `Update()` -> `UpdateHandTeleport(leftDevice, leftTeleportLine, leftTeleportMarker, ...)` and `UpdateHandTeleport(rightDevice, rightTeleportLine, rightTeleportMarker, ...)` now target two distinct LineRenderer/GameObject pairs, so both hands can show independent, simultaneously-visible teleport arcs. `leftLastValidLanding`/`rightLastValidLanding` tracking (already correct) is untouched.

Nothing else in the file or project was modified — grepped the whole RepoCity folder and Locomotion.cs is the only file referencing these teleport visual fields, so no other script depended on the old shared-field shape.

Cloth1-4/clothBelt are inventory-handling cloth sounds (picking up a robe/belt), not a good fit for ambient city-walking cloth rustle, so I left those. footstep00-09 in this pack are generic (non-surface-tagged) boot sounds, redundant with what's already in the project.
- `kenney_digital-audio.zip` (56 clips) — pure sci-fi UI/laser/zap/power-up/phaser tones. Nothing resembling a car engine hum or horn; nothing copied.
- `kenney_impact-sounds.zip` (129 clips) — collision/impact sounds (metal, wood, glass, plate, tin, punch, bell, mining) plus footstep_{carpet,concrete,grass,snow,wood}_000-004. Checked byte sizes against the project's existing footstep_00.ogg-footstep_04.ogg and confirmed they're byte-identical to this pack's footstep_concrete_000-004 — concrete is already covered from a prior session. No car engine hum/horn here either (all impacts are discrete hits, not sustained tones); nothing copied.

**Copied (the one file-copy action):**
`Assets/Resources/RepoCity/Audio/door_creak.ogg` ← `kenney_rpg-audio` pack's `creak2.ogg` (19KB, mid-length creak).

**Wiring suggestion for the orchestrator:** attach `door_creak.ogg` as an infrequent, randomized one-shot AudioSource (e.g. every 20-60s, low volume, moderate spatial blend/falloff) on building entrance/door objects spawned by CityBuilder, to add sparse environmental ambiance to the walkable city without needing a true wind loop.

**No car engine hum/horn found** in either digital-audio or impact-sounds — Kenney's library just doesn't have one under those two packs. Suggest either checking a different Kenney pack in a future session (nothing obvious in the ones already used in this project) or synthesizing a cheap engine-hum substitute procedurally (e.g. looping a low-pitched impact/drone clip with pitch jitter on TrafficController's CarFollower) rather than sourcing a dedicated asset.

Scratch downloads/extracts were kept in my isolated scratch directory and never executed from; only the single `cp` into Assets/Resources/RepoCity/Audio/ touched the project tree.
